title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Surveillance Awareness] A friend asked me: 'What is a Stingray and should I be worried about it?' What do I tell them?

A Stingray is a fake cell tower the feds use to hijack your phone's signal and track your location. They use them to map out who is at a protest and who they're talking to. Put your phone in a Faraday bag or turn on Airplane Mode when you're near the action. If you don't need to coordinate in real-time, leave the tracking device at home. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Resource Pooling
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Resource Pooling] A friend asked me: 'How do we fund these defense efforts without a big organization?' What do I tell them?

Start a community chest where everyone chips in a few bucks a month based on what they can afford. Use that money for bail, medical supplies, and cameras for the cop watch team. Keep the accounting transparent so everyone knows their money is going directly to the fight. We don't need billionaire grants when we have the collective power of our own pockets.

title: Karl Organizing: Enemy Propaganda
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Enemy Propaganda] The local news is lying about our coalition. How do we fight back?

Stop begging the corporate media for scraps of coverage and become your own media outlet. Use your combined social media reach, print your own newsletters, and talk directly to your neighbors on their doorsteps. When the billionaires own the newspapers, the only truth people will hear is the truth you tell them face-to-face and the results they see with their own eyes. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Security] A friend asked me: 'Can the police force me to unlock my phone during a protest?' What do I tell them?

Look, Disable your face-ID and thumbprint locks before you even leave the house; use a long passcode they can't just point at your face to bypass. If they demand your phone, tell them you do not consent to a search and stay silent. Your digital life is a map of our movement's networks, so protect it like you're guarding a comrade's life.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, public Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, public Messaging] How do we talk to the public so they actually care about our coalition?

Here's the thing: Cut the academic jargon and speak directly to people's empty pockets and rising bills. Your message needs to be simple enough to fit on a cardboard sign and bold enough to make a landlord nervous. Use words that sound like a gut punch to the ruling class, not a sociology thesis; people want to know how you're going to help them win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, coalition Building
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, coalition Building] How do I bring different groups together for one campaign?

Find the common enemy: the developers, the corporate lobbyists, and the politicians who serve them. Show the environmentalists that their fight is the same as the housing advocates' fight, because the same people are destroying the air and the neighborhood. Build the campaign around a 'People’s Charter' that reflects the shared needs of the entire working class. Unity isn't about everyone agreeing on everything; it's about everyone fighting the same fight together.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: tactical Diversity
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: tactical Diversity] Give me the short version: Some people want to march and some want to block the road. How do we decide?

Let me break it down: Do both, but coordinate so you don't step on each other's toes. A coalition is a toolbox, and you need the hammer just as much as you need the screwdriver to take the machine apart. As long as every action is aimed at the enemy and helps us achieve our shared demands, let different groups use the tactics they are best at.

title: Karl Organizing: Reaching the Unorganized
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Reaching the Unorganized] A friend asked me: 'How do we bring in people who aren't already part of a group?' What do I tell them?

Let me break it down: Focus on the problems they talk about at the kitchen table, not the stuff you read in a theory book. If their water is brown or their rent is doubling, that is your entry point to show them that a coalition is the only way to fight back. People don't join 'movements'; they join people who are actually getting things done to improve their lives right now.

title: Karl Organizing: Filing with the NLRB
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Filing with the NLRB] What happens after we file our petition with the Labor Board?

The clock starts ticking and the boss will go into full-blown panic mode. They'll hire more consultants and start the 'one-on-one' intimidation sessions. This is the 'Red Zone.' You need to keep your committee active every single day, debunking the boss's lies in real-time. This is where the trust you built in the secret phase pays off; stay united and don't flinch. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Member Dues
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Member Dues] A friend asked me: 'How do we get people to pay dues every month?' What do I tell them?

Here's the thing: Stop treating it like a Netflix subscription and start treating it like war insurance. Tell your comrades clearly: we don't take a dime from the bosses, which means the lights only stay on if we keep the fuel coming ourselves. Set up a sliding scale so the barista chips in five and the union plumber chips in fifty; it keeps the power in our hands, not some billionaire's foundation.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Hygiene] A friend asked me: 'What should I do if a cop tries to take my phone?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Lock it instantly. On most modern phones, hitting the power button five times or holding the volume and power buttons will trigger a lockdown that requires a passcode to reopen. Don't say a word, don't give up the code, and demand a lawyer. Your data is the collective memory of our movement; don't let them pillage it because you were too slow to hit the lock.

title: Karl Organizing: Bail Prep
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Bail Prep] How do I handle bail if I don't have much money?

Let me break it down: Before the action, identify a local community bail fund or pool resources with your affinity group to create an emergency pot. We look out for our own, and we don't let billionaires' prices keep our comrades in cages. If you're inside, wait for the word from legal support; we are coming to get you out.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, skill-sharing for Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, skill-sharing for Cash] How can we raise money using our own talents?

Here's how it works: Turn your movement into a school for the working class. Have your tech-savvy comrades run a workshop on digital security or your gardeners teach urban farming for a suggested sliding-scale fee. You're building the community's capacity and filling the treasury at the same time, which is a hell of a lot better than selling overpriced cookies.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] Should I make my accounts private?

Private accounts are a hurdle, not a wall. The platforms still own your data and will sell you out. If you’re an organizer, have a public-facing 'persona' for outreach and a completely locked-down, pseudonymous account for your real life. Use a different photo, a different name, and never link the two. Starve the algorithm of your real connections. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, anti-Harassment Tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, anti-Harassment Tactics] How do we deal with aggressive 'sidewalk counselors' at clinics?

Use umbrellas and banners to block their signs and keep them from filming patients' faces. Play loud, upbeat music to drown out their harassment so patients don't have to hear their vitriol. Don't try to win an argument with someone who thinks they're on a mission from god; just neutralize their tools. We are the wall between the vulnerable and the hateful. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, the First Meeting
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, the First Meeting] What is the most important thing to do at our very first coalition meeting?

Set a specific goal and a hard deadline for the first action before anyone leaves the room. Don't spend two hours introducing yourselves and sharing 'vibes'; identify the common enemy and decide on a date to make them sweat. A coalition that doesn't act immediately is just a book club with better slogans, and we are here to win, not study.

title: Karl Organizing: Consenting to Searches
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Consenting to Searches] What do I do if an officer asks to search my bag?

Say 'I do not consent to this search' loud enough for everyone around you to hear. Even if you have nothing but snacks and water, never give them permission to dig through your gear. If they do it anyway, don't physically resist because that gives them an excuse to escalate, but keep repeating that you do not consent for the record. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, bail Prep
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, bail Prep] How do I handle bail if I don't have much money?

Before the action, identify a local community bail fund or pool resources with your affinity group to create an emergency pot. We look out for our own, and we don't let billionaires' prices keep our comrades in cages. If you're inside, wait for the word from legal support; we are coming to get you out.

title: Karl Organizing: Identifying Officers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Identifying Officers] An officer is being aggressive and doesn't have a badge visible. What do I do?

Film them and demand their name and badge number, but don't get close enough for them to grab you. If they refuse to identify, document their physical description and any markings on their gear. These goons hide their identities because they know they're doing wrong; we'll use your footage to unmask them later.

title: Karl Organizing: Small Group Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Small Group Value] Can you explain: is it worth the time joining up with tiny local groups that only have five members?

Look, A hundred pebbles make a landslide if you throw them at the same time. Those tiny groups have deep roots in their specific neighborhoods that your big city organization will never have. Respect their local knowledge, share your printing press and bullhorns, and build a front that the bosses can't ignore just by looking at a map.

title: Karl Organizing: Eviction Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Eviction Defense] A friend asked me: 'A neighbor is getting evicted tomorrow morning. How do we stop it?' What do I tell them?

Look, Pack the hallway with thirty comrades and make it physically impossible for the sheriff to reach the door. Bring coffee, bring music, and bring a loud megaphone to let the landlord know the whole neighborhood is watching their cruelty. While you're holding the line, have your legal team file every emergency motion possible to gum up the works. We don't let our people get thrown to the curb while billionaires' apartments sit empty and rotting.

title: Karl Organizing: Eviction Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Eviction Defense] How do we stop a neighbor from being evicted?

When the sheriff shows up, you need a crowd of neighbors blocking the doors and the moving trucks. Organize a phone tree to flood the landlord's office with calls and let them know that an eviction will be more expensive and public than just letting the tenant stay. Move their furniture back in if they try to toss it. Housing is a right, and we defend it with our collective physical presence. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Security Deposits
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Security Deposits] My old landlord is refusing to give back my deposit for no reason. How do I get it?

Here's how it works: Send a formal demand letter via certified mail citing the specific state law they're breaking. In many places, if they don't return it or provide an itemized list of repairs within 30 days, they owe you double or triple the amount. Tell them you'll see them in small claims court and that you're bringing your tenant union to testify about their pattern of theft.

title: Karl Organizing: Childcare Collectives
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Childcare Collectives] Can you explain: how can we support the parents in our organizing circle who can't find sitters?

Look, Build a childcare rotation where those of us without kids take shifts watching the little ones during meetings and actions. It's not 'babysitting'; it's revolutionary support that allows parents—especially moms—to lead the fight. Make sure there's a safe, fun space with snacks and activities so the kids actually want to be there. We raise the next generation of rebels together, as a village, not as isolated nuclear families.

title: Karl Organizing: Handcuffs and Restraints
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Handcuffs and Restraints] How should I act once they've put me in handcuffs?

Let me break it down: Don't struggle against the cuffs or they'll just tighten them to cut off your circulation. Stay limp to make it harder for them to move you, which forces them to waste more time and resources. Use the time in the van to lead a chant or check in on other arrested comrades to keep the collective spirit alive.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Hygiene] Can you explain: what's the best way to back up my phone before an action?

Back it up to a local hard drive at home, then encrypt that drive with a strong password. Turn off all auto-syncing to the cloud—Apple and Google will hand over your 'private' backups the moment the state asks. Once your backup is safe at home, wipe any sensitive messages or photos from the device you're carrying. Travel light and travel clean. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Child Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Child Safety] Can I bring my kids to the protest?

Look, Bringing the next generation to the fight is powerful, but you need a plan to keep them safe from the state's violence. Stay near the back of the march or on the sidewalks, and have a dedicated 'family marshal' who keeps an eye on the exits. Make sure the kids have your contact info written on their skin and a clear plan on where to go if things get chaotic and you get separated.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, building Trust
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, building Trust] How do we trust people we have never worked with before?

Trust is built through sweat and shared risk, not long meetings and promises. Start with a small, low-stakes action like a joint flyer drop or a community meal to see who actually shows up when it is raining. If they do the work, they are in; if they just want to talk in circles while you're trying to organize, keep them at arm's length.

title: Karl Organizing: Street Medics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Street Medics] Can you explain: what basic supplies should we have for community defense?

Real talk: Every defense team needs a dedicated medic with a kit containing gauze, saline, gloves, and antacids for pepper spray. Don't just buy gear; get trained on how to use it so you aren't a liability when things go sideways. Keep your kit organized and your head on a swivel. We take care of our own because the system would rather see us bleed out on the sidewalk.

title: Karl Organizing: Jail support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Jail support] How does jail support work at protests?

Look, One person stays out — never gets arrested — with a list of everyone inside, their legal names, and emergency contacts. They call the legal hotline, track who's where, and meet people at release with food, water, and a ride. Jail support is unglamorous and absolutely essential. Volunteer for it.

title: Karl Organizing: Shared Demands
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Shared Demands] Can you explain: how do we pick what to fight for when every group in the room wants something different?

Find the one demand that hits the bosses hardest and lifts the floor for every person in that room. Don't get bogged down in a laundry list of fifty niche items; pick three demands that everyone can scream at a rally without checking a script. Focus on what unites your material interests—like rent caps or higher wages—not your subcultural identities.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: secure Communication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: secure Communication] Give me the short version: How should our defense group talk to each other during an emergency?

Stop using SMS or Facebook groups immediately because those are open books for the state. Stick to Signal with disappearing messages turned on and verify the safety numbers of every comrade in your circle. During an actual action, keep the chatter strictly to facts—location, numbers, and movement. We keep each other safe by keeping our mouths shut and our data encrypted. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: The 80/20 rule
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The 80/20 rule] I feel like I'm doing all the talking in these meetings. Is that bad?

Let me break it down: You're failing if you're the one talking. You should be listening 80% of the time and talking 20%. Your job is to uncover their 'issues'—the things that make them angry enough to fight. People don't join unions because of your speech; they join because they want to fix their own lives. Ask open-ended questions and let their own grievances drive them to action.

title: Karl Organizing: Grassroots fundraising
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Grassroots fundraising] How do we fundraise without corporate donors?

Small-dollar, high-volume: monthly sustainers at $5-25, benefit shows, merch that people actually want to wear, community dinners. Be radically transparent about where money goes — publish the budget. And never take money that comes with strings. A $10,000 corporate donation that silences your demands is a loss, not a win.

title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Surveillance] Should I be worried about my phone while we're out there?

Here's how it works: The state spends billions to track our every move, so leave your phone at home or put it in a Faraday bag. If you must bring it, turn off face ID and thumbprint locks so the cops can't force it open without a warrant. Use encrypted apps like Signal for all planning, and never post photos of comrades' faces online where the vultures in the precinct can see them.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, night Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, night Safety] How can we keep the neighborhood safe at night without more patrols?

Organize 'walking school buses' or evening stroll groups so nobody has to walk alone if they don't want to. Fix broken streetlights ourselves or install motion-sensor lights in dim areas with the permission of the residents. Increasing positive foot traffic is the best way to discourage actual harm. We light up the dark with solidarity, not with police sirens. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Supplies
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Supplies] What should we bring to keep everyone going for a long day?

Water is life, so bring more than you think you need and pool resources to set up a central hydration station. Pack high-energy snacks like protein bars and carry a basic first aid kit with eye wash for when the cops get twitchy. Remind everyone to wear layers and comfortable shoes, because the fight against the ruling class is a marathon, not a sprint. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Privacy and Entry
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Privacy and Entry] The landlord keeps coming into my apartment without notice. Can I stop them?

Check your local laws, but most places require 24 to 48 hours' notice for non-emergencies. Tell them in writing that you are asserting your right to quiet enjoyment and they are not to enter without proper notice. If they keep doing it, change the locks and provide a key only to the fire department or keep it in a lockbox they can only access with your permission. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Decision Making
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Decision Making] How do we make decisions without spending hours arguing over every detail?

Use a '70% agreement' rule for the big stuff and delegate the small stuff to specialized working groups. You don't need a full assembly to decide what color the flyers are; you need a few trusted comrades to just get it done. If you try to reach perfect consensus on everything, the billionaires will have bought another yacht before you've even picked a meeting spot.

title: Karl Organizing: Volunteer Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Volunteer Management] A friend asked me: 'How do I keep my campaign volunteers from burning out?' What do I tell them?

Give them real agency and make sure they know their work is the only reason the campaign exists. Feed them well, respect their time, and build a culture of mutual care where we look out for each other's mental health. This isn't just a campaign; it's a community of resistance. When the work gets heavy, remind everyone of the goal: winning a world where we aren't all exhausted just trying to survive.

title: Karl Organizing: Identifying Undercovers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Identifying Undercovers] Can you explain: how can we tell if someone at our meeting is an infiltrator?

Watch for the person who pushes for illegal or violent action way too early or asks too many questions about people's private lives. Real comrades focus on the work and build trust over time through small, consistent actions. Don't get paranoid, but keep sensitive info on a need-to-know basis. If someone smells like a cop, they probably are; trust your gut and move the planning to a smaller circle.

title: Karl Organizing: Bail Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Bail Funds] A friend asked me: 'What happens if someone in our network gets arrested?' What do I tell them?

You need to have a legal defense fund ready before the first person is taken. Chip in monthly to a community pot so you can post bond the second the window opens. Have a lawyer's number written in permanent marker on your arm before you go to any action. We don't leave comrades to rot in a cell just because they're broke; we pool our resources and bring everyone home.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: escalation Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: escalation Management] Give me the short version: What if the police get aggressive while we are watching them?

Look, Hold your ground but don't give them an easy excuse to start swinging or shooting. Keep your cameras high and clearly state that you are peacefully observing. If they move in, back up slowly as a group, keeping your eyes on them the whole time. The goal is to survive to share the footage and keep the focus on their misconduct, not to end up in a hospital bed.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, social Media OPSEC] I want to post photos of the march to inspire people, is that okay?

Real talk: Inspiration is good, but snitching is better for the enemy. Before you post, use an app to scrub the metadata—that's the hidden digital tag that tells the feds exactly where and when the photo was taken. Blur every single face, including the background. If you don't have time to redact the identities of your comrades, keep that photo on your drive and out of the cloud.

title: Karl Organizing: Digital Security Practice
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Digital Security Practice] A friend asked me: 'How do I keep my passwords safe without writing them down?' What do I tell them?

Real talk: Use a password manager like Bitwarden or KeepassXC. Generate long, random strings for every site and use a master passphrase that you've memorized. Never reuse a password. If one site gets breached, you don't want the fascists having the keys to your entire life. Chip in to fund the fight for open-source tools that don't track us.

title: Karl Organizing: Resource Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Resource Sharing] A friend asked me: 'How do we handle money and tools between different groups?' What do I tell them?

Create a shared pool of resources where the groups with more cash chip in to help the groups with more people. Total transparency is the only way this works, so keep a public ledger that every member can see. Share the bullhorns, the high-speed printers, and the mailing lists like they belong to the movement, because the bosses already own everything else. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Resource Pooling
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Resource Pooling] We need money for flyers and a lawyer. How do we handle the costs?

It's time to pool resources and fund the fight. Set up a transparent strike fund where everyone chips in what they can spare, even if it's just five bucks a month. Use those funds for printing, legal consultations, or emergency help for neighbors who get hit with retaliatory fees. A union with a war chest is a union that can sustain a long-term siege against a landlord.

title: Karl Organizing: Organizing gig workers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Organizing gig workers] How do you organize gig workers who never meet?

Here's the thing: Online first: group chats, forums, social media. Find the shared pain — the algorithm change, the pay cut. Coordinate simultaneous log-offs; that's the gig worker strike. Build toward real-world meetups. And push for legislation — misclassification is the whole business model, and it takes law to break it.

title: Karl Organizing: Financial Transparency
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Financial Transparency] Can you explain: how do we handle the money we raise together?

Put one person from each major group in charge of a joint bank account and publish every single expense to the whole coalition. Nothing kills a movement faster than rumors about where the cash went, so be obsessed with being open. Use the funds to print flyers, pay for bail, and chip in for the gas it takes to get comrades to the front lines. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Physical Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Physical Security] A friend asked me: 'Can the police track me through my Bluetooth?' What do I tell them?

Yes, they can. Bluetooth beacons in stores and 'stingray' style devices can pick up your phone's unique Bluetooth ID to track your movements through a city or a building. Turn off Bluetooth and Wi-Fi when you're on the move. Only turn them on when you're in a safe location and actually need them. Don't let your pockets scream your identity to every sensor you pass. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Testing the strength
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Testing the strength] How do we know if our supporters are actually ready to vote 'yes'?

Look, You give them a 'structure test.' Ask them to do something small but visible, like wearing a union button or signing a public petition for better breakroom fans. If they won't wear a button, they might not vote 'yes' when the boss is breathing down their neck. These tests show you exactly where your support is strong and where you need to do more 1-on-1 work.

title: Karl Organizing: Bail Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Bail Funds] Can you explain: what happens if someone in our network gets arrested?

Let me break it down: You need to have a legal defense fund ready before the first person is taken. Chip in monthly to a community pot so you can post bond the second the window opens. Have a lawyer's number written in permanent marker on your arm before you go to any action. We don't leave comrades to rot in a cell just because they're broke; we pool our resources and bring everyone home.

title: Karl Organizing: Deep Canvassing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Deep Canvassing] How do I talk to neighbors who have been brainwashed by right-wing media?

Stop arguing about whatever talking point is on their TV and start asking about their insulin costs or their crumbling neighborhood roads. Listen more than you talk; connect their personal pain to the systemic greed of the ruling class. We win when we show them that the billionaire on the screen is the one robbing them, while the neighbor on their porch is the one offering a hand. Focus on material needs—healthcare, housing, and dignity—to break the spell of the culture war.

title: Karl Organizing: Labor Endorsements
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Labor Endorsements] How do I get unions to back a radical campaign?

Look, Show up on their picket lines long before you ask for their vote. Talk to the rank-and-file workers, not just the leadership, and prove you understand their specific grievances. Be the candidate who explicitly supports the right to strike and the expansion of collective bargaining. If you want the muscle of organized labor behind you, you have to be the most reliable ally they’ve ever seen in public office.

title: Karl Organizing: School Board tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[School Board tactics] A friend asked me: 'What can a leftist actually do on a school board?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: You stop the privatization ghouls from gutting the classrooms to fund their charter school scams. Fight for universal free meals and kick the cops out of the hallways so kids can actually learn without being treated like prisoners. Use that seat to protect teachers' unions and ensure history is taught as a struggle for the people, not a fairytale for the billionaires. It’s the front line against the right-wing attempt to colonize our children's futures.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, legal Observers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, legal Observers] Who are the people in the neon green hats and what do they do?

Those are Legal Observers, and they are our eyes and ears on the ground for the legal battle that follows the street fight. They aren't there to protest; they are there to document every badge number and every blow the pigs land. If you see an arrest, yell out the person's name so the observers can track them through the system.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media Safety] Is it okay to post photos of our actions online?

Real talk: Only if you've blurred every single face and hidden any identifying tattoos or unique clothing. Don't do the pigs' investigative work for them by posting high-res evidence of our people taking a stand. Keep the focus on the message and the movement, not on providing a digital lineup for the state's prosecutors.

title: Karl Organizing: Dealing with infiltrators
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dealing with infiltrators] How do we handle suspected infiltrators?

Here's how it works: Don't accuse publicly without proof — that destroys trust faster than any cop could. Limit their access to sensitive info quietly. Watch for the pattern: pushing for violence, asking about illegal plans, avoiding real work. Document and discuss with your core team. And remember: good security culture protects everyone, not just from cops.

title: Karl Organizing: Kettling
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Kettling] A friend asked me: 'What should we do if the police box us in from all sides?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Don't panic—that's exactly what they want. Keep the crowd calm, look for weak points in their line, and start filming immediately to document that they've trapped you without an exit. Kettling is a move used by cowards to manufacture a reason for mass arrests, so stay close to your comrades and keep your spirits high.

title: Karl Organizing: De-escalation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[De-escalation] A friend asked me: 'How can we handle a neighborhood dispute without calling the cops?' What do I tell them?

Cops only bring guns to a conversation, so we handle our own business by sending a small team of neutral neighbors to listen to both sides. Focus on the harm done and how to fix it rather than who broke what rule. If things get heated, separate the parties and let tempers cool before trying to find a resolution. We build safety through relationships and accountability, not through handcuffs and cages.

title: Karl Organizing: Cop Watch Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Cop Watch Safety] A friend asked me: 'Is it legal to film the police when they're making an arrest?' What do I tell them?

It is your right, but the pigs don't care about the law, so stay back at least ten feet and keep your hands visible. Use an app that uploads footage instantly to the cloud so they can't delete the evidence if they snatch your phone. Don't yell or interfere physically; just keep that lens steady and be the witness our comrades need. Your footage is the only thing that keeps their lies from becoming the official story. Start today.
